narratives.Overview:
docs(agents,skills): always-on pin policy — critical skills referenced from AGENTS.md to reduce false negatives

## Summary

antfu notes AGENTS.md can outperform skills because it always loads, while on-demand skills have false negatives. Mitigation: reference must-apply skills from AGENTS.md. Directive routes many skills via triggers but lacks an explicit tier: always-pin vs on-demand vs never-pin.

## The gap

Process-critical skills (implementation intent / pre-pr / review-cycle / swarm gates) may not load if the agent fails to match triggers. No documented pin list or criteria for what must be always-on.

## Proposed approach

1. Define tiers:
   - always-pin: named in AGENTS.md (or consumer AGENTS) as required load for matching work types
   - on-demand: trigger keywords only
   - reference-only: external or rare
2. Publish default pin set for directive development and for consumer installs
3. Document that pins are for false-negative-sensitive process, not for entire language docs (those stay on-demand)
4. Optional: catalog field alwaysPin: true

## Proposed changes

- AGENTS.md / templates/agents-entry.md pin section
- skills catalog or conventions
- setup skill: consumer AGENTS gets recommended pins

## Acceptance criteria

- Pin tiers documented
- Default pin list for directive process skills exists
- Explicit anti-pattern: pinning entire framework/doc skill packs into AGENTS.md
